targetText: But it is not a state organisation; nor is it one designed for coercion, but for education. It is an organisation designed to draw in and to train; it is, in fact, a school: a school of administration, a school of economic management, a school of communism.
summary: Lenin defines the trade union under the dictatorship of the proletariat as an educational institution rather than a coercive state body, designed to train workers in management and cultivate communist consciousness.
context: Trotsky had proposed the administrative incorporation and militarization of trade unions at the conclusion of the Civil War, which Lenin opposed as a bureaucratic overreach that would alienate the working masses.

targetText: It can be exercised only by a vanguard that has absorbed the revolutionary energy of the class. The whole is like an arrangement of cogwheels. Such is the basic mechanism of the dictatorship of the proletariat, and of the essentials of transition from capitalism to communism.
summary: Lenin illustrates how proletarian state power operates through interconnected mechanisms: the revolutionary vanguard party provides political direction, while mass trade unions serve as the transmission mechanism to the broader working class.

targetText: politics is the most concentrated expression of economics
summary: Lenin emphasizes that economic tasks cannot be solved without a sound political foundation, meaning political leadership and class orientation must take precedence over narrow technocratic planning.

targetText: our application of coercion was correct and successful whenever we had been able to back it up from the start with persuasion
summary: Lenin formulates a central principle of socialist governance: state authority and discipline are only effective and justifiable when grounded in patient political explanation and mass consent.

targetText: The sum and substance of his policy is bureaucratic harassment of the trade unions.
summary: Lenin warns against administrative bullying and top-down interference in working-class organizations, asserting that commanding workers by fiat damages the vitality of the socialist state.
